integrity: The Tanner publication record was checked for the exact day-resolved 1975 public date and foundational predator–prey scope. The Braza same-model record was checked for the two-Hopf bifurcation theorem and primary MSC 34C25. A complete open 2014 Holling–Tanner article was inspected through its model description, positive-invariance and equilibrium discussion, literature review, canard analysis, and biological interpretation; targeted complete-text searches found no conditional, variance, average, or stationary formulation matching the accepted theorem. Published semantic searches covered invariant measures, conditional nullcline regressions, harmonic prey calibration, stationary covariance/variance, support bounds, and activity defects. The two conditional laws, support ceiling, fiberwise prey-excess identity, variance decompositions, equality rigidity, and nullcline crossings were independently reconstructed and replayed with the packaged exact checker.
scientific_limitations: The theorem assumes compact invariant support strictly inside the positive quadrant.
Boundary equilibria and extinction-axis invariant measures are excluded.
The model has constant positive parameters and no delays, harvesting, diffusion, stochastic forcing, or feedback control.
The result determines selected conditional moments and variance defects rather than the full invariant distribution, cycle period, or extrema.
The 1997 two-limit-cycle source was compared through its bibliographic record and accessible statement material rather than blanket full-text noncoverage.
An equivalent short weighted generator identity could remain in older unindexed predator–prey literature.
title: Fiberwise carrying-capacity excess and nullcline activity in the Holling–Tanner oscillator
